title: Civil Asset Forfeiture Expansion - Police Profit Incentives and Property Seizure Without Conviction
description_short: Civil Asset Forfeiture Expansion - Police Profit Incentives and Property Seizure Without Conviction

Those examples concern local systems, not a Trump administration expansion.

title: Trump: FHA blacklists Fred Trump after Senate profiteering investigation
description_short: Trump: FHA blacklists Fred Trump after Senate profiteering investigation
description_medium: The supplied timeline says a Senate committee investigated Fred Trump and more than 30 other developers over profits from Federal Housing Administration-backed apartment projects. It reports that Trump and a partner received at least $3.5 million more than the complexes cost to build. The material documents an allegation and inquiry; it does not establish a blacklist order or the committee’s final findings.
description_long: The supplied source summary says a Senate committee examined Fred Trump and more than 30 real-estate developers in 1954 over alleged profiteering connected to Federal Housing Administration financing. It reports that Fred Trump and a partner received at least $3.5 million more from the FHA-backed apartment projects than the cost of construction. The allegation concerned how federal housing support was used and whether developers had earned excessive returns from projects financed through the program. The supplied record does not include the committee’s complete findings, a response from Fred Trump, or an agency document showing that the FHA formally blacklisted him. It therefore supports an account of an investigation and the reported financial disparity, not a conclusion that a specific sanction followed or that the allegation was finally adjudicated. The earlier title asserted that the FHA blacklisted Fred Trump, a step not established by the available material. The revised title keeps the focus on the Senate inquiry and frames profiteering as an allegation. A committee report or FHA decision would be needed to describe the outcome.

title: Trump: Journalist warns organized crime infiltrating U.S., Israel, and Europe threatens democracy
description_short: Trump: Journalist warns organized crime infiltrating U.S., Israel, and Europe threatens democracy
description_medium: Journalist Robert I. Friedman’s 2000 book Red Mafiya warned that Russian organized crime could use global business and political connections to penetrate institutions in the United States, Israel and Europe. The book presented that as a threat to democracy, not proof that a particular government had been captured.
description_long: In Red Mafiya, his 2000 investigation of Russian organized crime, journalist Robert I. Friedman warned that criminal networks were expanding their reach across business and government in the United States, Israel and Europe. He argued that this transnational influence could threaten democratic institutions. Friedman had spent years reporting on Russian organized crime, and the book became a major account of its growth and connections. His warning addressed how illicit networks might exploit legitimate commerce and political relationships; it was not a claim that every institution in the regions named had been captured. The work belongs to the broader history of reporting on post-Soviet criminal organizations and their international activity. Friedman died in 2002. The event is the publication and argument of his book, which framed organized crime as a political as well as law-enforcement concern. Specific present-day cases or government links require their own evidence and are not established by the book’s general warning.
notes: The linked New York Times archive page is a 2000 report on a money-laundering investigation, not Robert Friedman's book or the warning attributed to him. The TrumpFile page was inaccessible in the prior review. A source for Friedman's exact argument and any intended Trump connection is still needed.
